public_rationale: The sources establish capital spending and a substantial AWS–Anthropic infrastructure relationship. They do not show what fraction of total spending serves the two labs. Dedicated projects cannot establish an overwhelming share without a complete denominator and an allocation of shared assets. Nor does evidence of other uses establish that the labs' share is small.
limitations: Several relevant financial pages could not be read successfully.
Capacity, customer commitments and capital spending are different measures.
The finding remains unresolved under either a combined-provider or provider-by-provider reading.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The vast majority of hyperscaler capex exists to support OpenAI and Anthropic.

statement.excerpt: I’d also argue that the vast majority of their capex exists to support these two load-bearing failsons.

our_interpretation: Their refers to Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet. These two refers to OpenAI and Anthropic.
The plain reading concerns an overwhelming share of the three companies' combined capital expenditure, with provider-level allocations also relevant.
The denominator is total capex, not merely AI capex or selected dedicated projects.
I use April–June 2026, the latest completed reporting quarter before the post, for the ongoing spending assertion.
Vast majority means substantially more than half. I do not invent an exact percentage absent from the claim.
The allocation to the labs is an estimate inferred from the projects and relationships cited in context; it is not presented as a disclosed accounting line.
criteria.support_condition: A comparable allocation of total capital expenditure shows that an overwhelming share was incurred to serve OpenAI and Anthropic, including a defensible allocation of shared infrastructure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable allocations show that spending serving the two labs is not an overwhelming share of total capex. A share at or below half would clearly contradict the claim.
